name: Turnover Bridge
description: Turnover Bridge is a 2-player trick game (more related to Whist than Bridge). 52-card deck, 26 each. Layout: 12 face-down in row + 12 face-up on top + 2 secret hole cards. Spades permanently trump. Play face-up cards or hole cards. When face-up played, turn over card beneath. Win 14+ of 26 tricks. Information warfare: visible cards vs hidden cards.

Spades permanently trump. Play face-up cards or hole cards. When face-up played, turn over card beneath. Win 14+ of 26 tricks. Information warfare: visible cards vs hidden cards.

Turnover Bridge is a two-player trick-taking game in the Whist and Honeymoon Bridge family. Honeymoon Bridge refers to any two-player adaptation of Contract Bridge; documented variants include Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies, where dummy hands have face-down cards with face-up cards on top and playing a face-up card turns the card beneath face up. Turnover Bridge uses this turnover mechanic with a 12+12+2 layout per player and fixed spades trump. Whist, the classic English trick-taking game, originated in England and was widely played in the 18th and 19th centuries; two-player variants became popular for couples and casual play.
12 face-down in row + 12 face-up on top + 2 hidden hole cards.

items.text: Play to 100 points: Instead of first to 14 tricks, play to 100 points (1 point per trick won).
